newsitem.title: CHINA: FORECAST - China sees May retail sales up 13.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - China sees May retail sales up 13.4 pct.

text.p: China's retail sales are expected to rise 13.4 percent in May, continuing a trend of moderate growth, the Financial Daily said on Wednesday.

The newspaper, quoting the State Information Centre of the State Economic and Trade Commission, said total retail sales would reach 215.0 billion yuan ($25.9 billion) for the month, representing a rise of 12.4 percent, adjusted for inflation.
Retail sales climbed 13.6 percent, or 12.4 percent in real terms, in April.
An easing in the growth of disposable income in the first quarter of this year was expected to be reflected in the retail sales picture in May.

The disposable income of city and township residents was estimated at 1,446 yuan over the first quarter, up 6.7 percent from the year-ago period. The rate of increase during the period was down seven percentage points from the previous year.

Rural disposable incomes rose over the quarter but they showed even more evidence of slower growth. Incomes were 564 yuan, up five percent for a reduction in the rate of growth of 17 percentage points.
Strong investor interest in the nation's stock and bond markets was also putting a cap on growth in retail sales.
The number of new securities accounts opened in Beijing alone this year was 6.5 times greater than the total for the same period last year, the newspaper said.
The report also said that five major commercial banks issued a total of 75.95 billion yuan worth of non-tradeable bonds between March 1 and May 10. It gave no comparative figure.
The newspaper said retail sales in May were expected to show a rise of 14.1 percent in the cities and townships and 12 percent in rural areas.
Retail sales overall for the January-May period were forecast at 1,088.3 billion yuan, up 14.4 percent over the year ago period.
